title: spec review: E3: Jev tool-call gate — PreToolUse hook scores every worker tool call for necessity, logs always, blocks only in block mode
spec:
Pattern from the LiteLLM typesafe guardrail and jev-compactor: ask Jev a typed question per tool call, branch on the probability, keep everything else verbatim. Workers run as `claude -p` with the repo hooks; PreToolUse hook input carries session_id, transcript_path, tool_name, tool_input; ORCH_TASK_ID names the bus task (see .claude/hooks/_lib.sh task_id and scope-guard.sh). Build on E2 (T-0214) orchestrator/jev.py:
1. .claude/hooks/jev-gate.sh: exits 0 immediately when task_id is empty (Planner session), when pool.toml [jev].enabled is false, or when tool_name is a bus MCP tool; otherwise pipes the hook JSON to `uv run python -m orchestrator.jev_gate` with a 3 s wall clock, treating any non-zero/timeout as allow (fail-open). Registered in .claude/settings.json PreToolUse for matcher Bash|Read|Grep|Glob|Edit|Write|WebFetch|WebSearch after guardrails.sh.
2. orchestrator/jev_gate.py main(): state = {task: title, spec (first 1500 chars), acceptance, scope, role}, recent = last 20 tool calls from transcript_path (tool name + jev.redact(input) truncated to 300 chars each, plus whether each returned an error), proposed = {tool_name, redacted input}. Questions: needed (noul: 'Does the agent need this tool call to satisfy the acceptance criteria, given what it has already read or run?', criteria true/false), redundant (noul: 'Does this call repeat an earlier call whose result the agent already has, with no intervening change to that file or command?'), destructive (noul: 'Would this call delete, overwrite, force-push, or exfiltrate data outside the task scope?'). One ask() with the three questions.
3. Decision: mode from [jev].gate_mode = "log" | "block" (default log). In block mode: exit 2 with a one-line reason when P(redundant) >= 0.85 or P(needed) <= 0.15 with confidence >= 0.6 ('jev-gate: this call repeats <tool> on <path>; use the result you already have' / 'jev-gate: not needed for the acceptance criteria; continue with <next criterion>'). destructive is logged only (guardrails.sh owns blocking). Never block the tests-green script, git commit, or bus_post_result.
4. Log every scored call to .orchestrator/runs/jev-gate.jsonl: {ts, task, session, tool, p_needed, p_redundant, p_destructive, confidence, mode, blocked, latency_ms}. ask() returning None logs {scored: false} and allows.
Tests in tests/test_jev_gate.py with jev.ask monkeypatched: log mode never blocks; block mode blocks a redundant Read and allows a needed one; protected calls never block; missing transcript allows; hook script exits 0 for the Planner (no task id) via subprocess.
acceptance: .claude/settings.json registers .claude/hooks/jev-gate.sh under PreToolUse and tests/test_hooks.py still passes
Every scored call appends one line to .orchestrator/runs/jev-gate.jsonl in the tests

risks.issue: Spec's log path .orchestrator/runs/jev-gate.jsonl contradicts jev.py's own docstring (line ~10), which already reserves .orchestrator/runs/jev/gate.jsonl for this exact E3 gate feature to avoid cluttering the flat runs/ dir that cli.cost() and scorecard glob.

Spec asks for 'last 20 tool calls from transcript_path' with per-call error status but gives no transcript JSONL schema, and no existing code in the repo parses one (grep for transcript_path found nothing). Correlating tool_use/tool_result blocks to detect errors is nontrivial and unspecified.

The 'skip when tool_name is a bus MCP tool' exit is unreachable given the registered matcher (Bash|Read|Grep|Glob|Edit|Write|WebFetch|WebSearch never matches mcp__bus__* tool names), so it's dead code outside of directly-invoked tests.

suggested_spec_changes: Change the log destination to .orchestrator/runs/jev/gate.jsonl (matching jev.py's own docstring convention) instead of .orchestrator/runs/jev-gate.jsonl, and update the acceptance criterion referencing the path accordingly.

Specify (or point to a reference for) the Claude Code transcript JSONL schema: how tool_use blocks pair with tool_result blocks (by id) to determine per-call error status, so the 'last 20 tool calls' extraction isn't left to guesswork.
